current.summary: The first-floor bedroom, mid-works. Walls are a deep green, now covered in large white filler patches where cables were chased for the bedside wall lights and sockets and where the new en-suite wall was built; the new wall itself is bare plaster. The ceiling is the finest in the house: a deep ornate plaster cornice and a ceiling with raised moulded panel frames and rosettes, all white. Wooden-blade ceiling fan and a crystal chandelier. Floor: old patterned cement tiles in a different design from the floor above — a central carpet pattern with a scrolling floral border and plain tiles round the edge. Furniture: a matching burr-walnut suite — a large three-door wardrobe with a shaped mirror and a serpentine chest of drawers with a marble top — an ornate gilt rococo mirror, and two old trunks. Cage wall lights either side of the bed. Green panelled door and frame to the stairs. The opening to the en suite has its metal pocket-door frame fitted but no door or surround yet.

target.renderPrompt:
Edit this photo of a room in our house. Keep the exact camera angle and keep all the architecture exactly as it is — walls, room shape, windows, doors, beams, floor and fixed fittings. Do not add, move or remove anything structural, and do not change the furniture unless I say so below. Remove all clutter: tools, boxes, bags, dust sheets, loose cables, packaging, laundry and toiletries. Show the room finished and tidy.

Changes to make:
- Walls evenly painted in the same deep green, with no white filler patches.
- The ornate white plaster cornice and decorative ceiling stay white and clean.
- Keep the burr-walnut wardrobe and chest, the gilt mirror, the crystal chandelier, the wooden ceiling fan, the old trunks and the patterned tile floor, cleaned.
- Remove the dust sheets: show the bed neatly made with natural linen.
- The green door and frame freshly painted. The opening to the en suite has a white panelled pocket door in a finished frame.

Style: photorealistic interior photograph, natural light plus warm 2700K lamps, no people, no text or labels.
